links.outcome: LLM error detection versus human physicians and between competing domestic and international models on same reports
links.effect: Missed-diagnosis detection best 0.467, the one category where human physicians outperformed every model; domestic vs international detection did not differ (Δmacro-F1 = −0.011, P = 0.84).
links.quote: Missed-diagnosis detection was the universal weakness (best 0.467) and the one category where the human physicians outperformed every model.

links.outcome: Dissociation between error-detection macro-F1 and overall-score calibration (ICC) across models
links.effect: Macro-F1 0.356–0.667 and ICC 0.099–0.627, weakly correlated (ρ = 0.38, p = 0.18); strongest detector Claude-Opus-4.8 (0.667) calibrated poorly (0.491).
links.quote: Raw detection ability does not guarantee a trustworthy score, and domestic and international models differ by deployment-relevant profile rather than by overall performance rank; both essential distinctions for performing clinical nuclear-medicine QC.

unlisted_practices: Controlling for access channel (agent channel vs clean API) when benchmarking LLMs to avoid inflated performance
Comparing domestic versus international LLMs on cost and on-premise deployability

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance of multiple commercial and open-source LLMs on automated quality control and error detection in PET/CT reports, evaluating raw model performance and calibration across API/agent access modalities without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
